Why is communication important for a technical person?
Even the best technical work has little impact if it cannot be explained clearly; good communication helps others understand decisions, collaborate, and act on your ideas.

How should you explain a technical concept to a non-technical person?
Use plain language, avoid jargon, rely on analogies and concrete examples, and focus on what matters to them rather than the underlying implementation details.

Why is it important to adapt your explanation to your audience?
Different audiences have different background knowledge and goals, so tailoring the level of detail and vocabulary makes the explanation actually useful to them.

What is the curse of knowledge in technical communication?
The curse of knowledge is the difficulty experts have imagining what it is like not to know something, which can make their explanations too advanced for the listener.

How can analogies help in explaining technical ideas?
Analogies connect an unfamiliar concept to something the listener already understands, making abstract or complex ideas easier to grasp.

Why should you avoid unnecessary jargon?

How do you know if your explanation was understood?

What is active listening?

Why are clarifying questions important?

What is the difference between an open and a closed question?
